The fifth hymn, consisting of fifteen verses beginning with “amīṣām indraḥ,” is the seerly composition of Vasukrapta (also known as Vasukarṇa) and is addressed to the Viśvedevas.
The fifteenth [verse] is a *triṣṭubh*, and the remaining ones are *jagatīs*.

Thus it is stated in the *Anukramaṇī*: “*Agnir indraḥ*; [the hymn] has five fewer [verses], or rather Vāsukra; Vasukarṇa [composed it], ending in *triṣṭubh*. 1. In manuscript *bha*, “*avardhayat*” is absent.

Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Vāyu, Pūṣan, and Sarasvatī, acting in harmony; the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the lofty Sky, Soma, Rudra, Aditi, and Brahmaṇaspati. || 1 || Agni. Indra. Varuṇa. Mitra. Aryaman. Vāyu. Pūṣan. Sarasvatī. Acting in harmony (sajoṣasaḥ). The Ādityas. Viṣṇu. The Maruts. The Sky (svaḥ). The Great One (bṛhat). Soma. Rudra. Aditi. The Lord of Prayer (brahmaṇaspatiḥ). || 1 ||

The connection with the following verse is as follows: Agni and the others, Āditya and the others, Vabṛhat and Bṛhatī, Vasu, Dyaus, Soma, and the other gods—these Vasus, being joined together in harmony, fill the intermediate space (antarikṣa) by their own greatness.

O Indra and Agni, lords of the moving world, impelling one another in the slaying of Vṛtra with your own bodies, you who dwell together, have filled the great mid-air with your power; so too has Soma, adorned with clarity, putting forth his majesty. O Indra and Agni: in the slayings of Vṛtra; lords of the moving world (sartapatī); impelling one another (mithaḥ hinvānā); with your bodies (tanvā); dwelling together (samaukasā); the mid-air (antarikṣam); greatly (mahi); have filled (ā papruḥ); with your power (ojasā); Soma; adorned with clarity (ghṛtaśrīḥ); putting forth his majesty (mahimānam īrayan). || 2 ||
In the slayings of Vṛtra— that is, in battles for the destruction of Vṛtra;
or alternatively, the suffix *kyap* is used here in the sense of the object (*karman*), as is characteristic of Vedic usage.
"Vṛtrahatyā" refers to battles, so called because "vṛtrāṇi" (obstacles) or enemies are slain therein.

In those battles, O Vasiṣṭhas—meaning you who are weaving together, who are carrying away the enemies by means of the strength residing within you, and who are moving forward—you two lords of the good, the masters of the dwelling, Indra and Agni, who share a common abode, being of glorious splendor through the clarified butter (*ghṛta*) known as *vasatīvarī* water, and manifesting your own greatness by extending it and raising it up on all sides—both Soma and these [deities] have filled the great intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) with their own power (*ojas*). They fill it completely.
The root *prā* is used in the sense of filling.

For them—those great ones, the unassailable, who know the *ṛta* and increase the *ṛta*—I offer these songs of praise. May they, who possess wondrous wealth and whose armor is the waters, grant us gifts for our glorification, being well-disposed friends. For them—of those great ones, the unassailable, the knowers of *ṛta*, the increasers of *ṛta*—I offer this watchful praise. May they, who dwell in the waters, the ocean, the givers of wondrous wealth, grant us gifts for our glorification, being well-disposed friends.

I, the knower of *ṛta*, impel the hymns (*stoma*) toward you— those gods, Agni and the others, who are great by their own greatness, who are unassailable, who do not yield to others, who are unapproachable by enemies, and who have grown through the *ṛta*-increasing sacrifice (*ṛtavṛdh*). The root *ṛ* (in *ṛtavṛdh*) belongs to the *juhoty-ādi* class, meaning "to go" or "to reach."
Possessing wonderful wealth—that is, endowed with desirable riches—or rather, possessing abundant wealth characterized by horses and so forth; O gods, we [invoke] you who are in the waters.
*Ap* is a name for form;
[we invoke you] who possess form, who are ocean-like.
The suffix *vap* is added in the sense of possession according to the rule *arṇavaḥ salopaśca* (Pāṇini 5.2.109).
Those who rain upon the cloud possessing water (*udakavat*) are the Vasumitras, the gods who possess excellent friends. May they grant us wealth for the sake of honor among the people;
[the root] *rās* means "to give."

Supporting the sun, the mid-regions, the luminous spheres, heaven and earth, and the broad ground with their might—like two wings, the gods, the bounteous patrons and wise leaders, magnifying him, offer praise for the sake of man. *svarṇaram*, *antarikṣāṇi*, *rocanā*, *dyāvābhūmī* (heaven and earth), *pṛthivīm*, *skambhuḥ*, *ojasā*, *pakṣāḥ-iva*, *mahayantaḥ*, *surātayaḥ*, *devāḥ*, *stavante*, *manuṣāya*, *sūrayaḥ*. 4.
1. Of those who have gone, those who are going, and those who are to go; of those who have reached, those who are reaching, and those who are to reach.
Gold belongs to all; their respective actions [belong] to Naināra, the sun, and the intermediate spaces.
Between heaven and earth, in the middle, dwell—that is, they reside—the intermediate spaces.

The gods have supported—meaning they hold fast by their own power—the shining, radiant energies situated in the middle, namely Heaven and Earth (dyāvābhūmī), the broad earth, and the vast intermediate space (antarikṣa), as well as these [deities] beginning with Āditya.
The word *skambhu* is a verbal root (*dhātu*) from which the mantra is derived; it is here in the form of the perfect tense (*liṭ*).

Furthermore, like wings, they extend riches to the poor; for this very reason, magnifying them—that is, honoring the worshippers with wealth and other gifts—they are the "good-givers" (surātayaḥ), the "joyful givers" (mudānāḥ), and the "wise ones" (sūrayaḥ) who impel wealth toward every human being. These gods are praised; they are extolled at this sacrifice.
Bestow gifts upon Mitra and Varuṇa, who grant to the worshipper; they are the two sovereign kings who do not neglect the mind [of the pious].
Whose lofty domain shines by its own law, and between whose two worlds the two heaven-and-earth revolve like wheels.

Bestow gifts upon Mitra and Varuṇa, who give to the donor; they who, as sovereigns, do not neglect the mind; whose high domain shines by the power of their law; between whom both worlds, heaven and earth, turn like two wheels. 5.
Bestow wealth upon the donor, grant it to those who praise you, and to Mitra and Varuṇa; offer the oblations.
The root *śikṣ* means "to give.
O sovereigns, the two universal rulers of all, Mitra and Varuṇa, who do not neglect nor become heedless even in their inner mind (*manas*).
How much less so by external activity?
The root *yucch* means "to be negligent"; it belongs to the Bhūvādigaṇa.

Of those two, Mitra and Varuṇa, the great (bṛhat) body (dhāma)— that is, the physical form— shines forth perfectly by virtue of their own characteristic activity (dharmaṇā), such as the illumination of the world and so forth;
and of those two, there is no distress (nārthasī)—
[the term *nārthas* being explained as] "distress (*ārta*), begging (*yācñā*), exhaustion (*tāpa*), sovereignty (*aiśvarya*), and blessing (*āśis*)."
When they are entreated, both *rodasī*—that is, Heaven and Earth—become turned toward [the petitioner].
Or alternatively:
when they are prosperous through gods and men, those two *dyāvāpṛthivī* become turned toward them.
The meaning is that they become dependent upon that.
The cow who goes around the path, yielding her milk at the appointed place, the guardian of the rite from the enclosure—
proclaiming herself to Varuṇa the donor, may she give to the gods and to Vivasvat the biped.

The cow who goes around the place of worship, yielding milk at the appointed time, she who is the fulfiller of vows and free from blemish—proclaiming herself, let her offer with an oblation to Varuṇa the donor, to the gods, and to Vivasvat. 6.

This cow of mine, who yields milk, curd, and other products, the *vratinī*—the leader of the rite through the provision of the milk for the fast-milk (*vratapayaḥ*)—has come to the prepared, consecrated place of the fast-milk, the dwelling of the sacrifice. Without being warded off, without being hindered, she goes around and comes of her own accord, being proclaimed by me as she is introduced. May that cow, for the sake of Varuṇa who has given the oblation, and for the other gods such as Indra, and for me, Vivasvat who serves the gods with food, grant protection and bestow milk upon me, the giver of the offering.
From the root *dāś* in the sense of "giving," there is the augment *leṭ*.
Alternatively:

The word "gauh" (cow) belongs to the Mādhyamika [world], because it is seen in such passages as, "She who milks out milk and nourishment for us, may she, the delightful one, milk out nourishment for us" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8.100.11).
It should be applied [to the mantra] in the same manner as before, with that [world] as its referent.
The sky-dwellers, fire-tongued, increasers of Truth, sit pondering the womb of Truth;
having propped up the heavens with their might, they have fashioned the waters and, having generated the sacrifice, have measured it out within their own bodies.

1. Having reached heaven and earth, those dwelling in the sky, whose tongue is Agni, who increase the *ṛta*, sit contemplating the womb of *ṛta*. Having propped up the foundation, they have brought the waters by their might; having generated the sacrifice, they have measured it out within their own bodies. ||7||
*Divakṣasaḥ*: those who pervade the sky (*div*) by their own splendor; [the root] *akṣu* means "to pervade";
the form is derived with the suffix *asun*.
Alternatively, they are the bearers of heaven;
having Agni as their tongue,
they have him as their mouth, for they lick— that is, taste— the oblations with Agni.

The gods—increasers of *ṛta*, increasers of the sacrifice, or those who cause the sacrifice to prosper—sit waiting, reflecting upon and examining the womb, the place of origin, of *ṛta*, the sacrifice that has become reality; they abide everywhere.
Having propped up and supported the sky with their own power, they have brought about, or are bringing about, the waters that were previously waterless.
Then, having generated the sacrifice, the object of worship, and the oblation, they thoroughly cleanse—that is, they adorn—the body, their own self;
the meaning is that they consume the oblation.
The two ancient ones, dwelling together in the same abode in the womb of Cosmic Order, protect the fathers who have passed away;
Heaven and Earth, acting in harmony with Varuṇa, swell with ghee-filled milk for the mighty bull.

The two parents, dwelling together in the same abode, have been examined; they abide in the womb of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*). Heaven and Earth, acting in harmony with Varuṇa according to their sacred law, cause the ghee-rich milk to swell for the mighty bull.

These two, Heaven and Earth—dwelling all around, pervading everywhere; the parents of all, having become mother and father; therefore the first-born, sharing the same abode—dwell in every womb, that is, in the place of the sacrifice (*ṛta*); they are said to reside as its support, or they dwell within the two forms of the *havirdhāna* (the oblation-holders). Moreover, with equal rites, they [serve] Varuṇa, the great one worthy of worship, for that sacrifice.
This is an elliptical expression;
it refers to other gods as well who cause the milk— that is, water— to flow and swell,
for by means of water, food is produced.
Parjanya and Vāta, the showerers; Indra and Vāyu, the possessors of the city; Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman;
the Āditya gods and Aditi—we invoke those who are on earth, those who are in heaven, and those who are in the waters.

Parjanya and Vāta, the two bulls, the fillers of the city; Indra and Vāyu—we invoke Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the gods, the Ādityas, and Aditi; those who are on earth, those who are in heaven, and those who are in the waters. 9.
Parjanya and Vāta—Parjanya and Vāta, Parjanya and Vāyu; the two bulls, the showerers of desires;
the two possessors of *purīpa* (water)—*purīpa* meaning water—they possess it as their instrument of action; Indra and Vāyu, and Varuṇa and Aśvin—these exist everywhere by their own majesty.
Vāyu is mentioned together with Parjanya and Indra with reference to their shared functions.

We invoke these Ādityas, the gods, and Aditi, their mother, at this sacrifice; we call them hither. Furthermore, those gods who are terrestrial—belonging to the earth—and those who are celestial, born in heaven, and those who have arisen in the waters—that is, in the intermediate space—we invoke them all.

1. *ta*-and *bha1.2.4.6.8* read "they pervade"; *bha7* reads "as if they pervade heaven. 2. *ta*-and *bha1.9.4.6.8* interpret the meaning as "they win the oblation" (*havirjayanti*); *bha7* interprets the meaning as "they share the oblation" (*havirbhajante*). 3. *ta*-and *bha* read "possessing characteristics" (*lakṣaṇavat*).
4. *ga-ta-bha-‘aparjanyāvāta’* does not exist. 5. *bha-vāyūparjanyā*. 6. *ta1.2.3.6.7.8-bha-‘vṛṣabhau’* does not exist.
7. We also call them *ga*, *ta*, *na*, *pa*, and *ya*; we call that *bha*.

Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, and the Ṛbhus; those two divine Hotṛ-priests who bring [the sacrifice] for our well-being; Bṛhaspati, the consumer of Vṛtra, the wise one; and the Soma that is Indra’s power—we, as seekers of wealth, implore them. (10) O Ṛbhus—those who shine by means of *ṛta* (truth), or who shine widely with their own splendor—O wise ones, that Soma which they bring (*ohete*) for your well-being and exhilaration; it brings (*āvahati*), according to the root *ūh* belonging to the *bhū* class, [that which is desired]. Likewise, it brings Bṛhaspati, the very wise one, and Indra, the devourer of Vṛtra, the Asura. We, who partake of wealth (*dhanasāḥ*), implore (*īmahe*) that Soma which is Indra’s power; we beg for wealth. The verb *īmahe* has the sense of begging. From the root *īṅ* "to go," belonging to the *div* class, the suffix is elided according to the rule "in the Veda, [suffixes are] frequently [elided]. (10)

Generating the sacred word (*brahman*), the cow, the horse, the plants, the trees, the earth, the mountains, and the waters; causing the sun to rise in the sky, O bounteous ones; and releasing the noble ordinances upon the earth—[we pray for wealth]. *brahma*, *gām*, *aśvam*, *janayantaḥ*, *oṣadhīḥ*, *vanaspatīn*, *pṛthivīm*, *parvatān*, *apaḥ*, *sūryam*, *divi*, *rohayantaḥ*, *sudānavaḥ*, *āryā*, *vratā*, *visṛjantaḥ*, *adhi*, *kṣami* || 11 || The *brahman* is the means of increase and a constituent part [of sacrifice], for by means of fire all creatures increase. Generating these—the cow, the horse, and other such animals, as well as the plants, the trees, the vast earth, the mountains, the clouds that fill the world with rain, or the waters, or the atmosphere—and furthermore causing the sun, the Āditya, to ascend in the sky; those gods, the "bounteous" (*sudānavaḥ*) who give beautiful gifts; "upon the earth" (*adhi kṣami*)—here the vowel *ā* is elided according to the rule of *yogavibhāga* (Pāṇini 6.4.140)—they release, that is, spread abroad, the noble, excellent, and auspicious ordinances (*vratāni*), such as sacrifices and other rites, throughout the world. "We pray for wealth from them"—this is the ellipsis.

O Aśvins, you rescued Bhujyu from the ocean, the source of affliction; O Lords, you delivered Śyāva, the son of Vadhrimatī. You brought Kamadyū to Vimada; you bestowed Yava and Viṣṇāpū upon Viśvaka. O Aśvins—possessors of horses, pervading all—O divine ones, from the ocean, the source of harm (*ahaṃsaḥ*), you rescued (*pipṛthaḥ*) Bhujyu, your protégé, the son of [Vadhryaśva], by name; you carried him across and protected him thoroughly. [The root] *pṛ* means "to protect" or "to fill"; it belongs to the *juhotyādi* class. The Vedic citation is: "You carried him across the ocean, the place of distress" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.118.6). Likewise, you gratified (*ajinavatam*) Śyāva—the son of Vadhrimatī, known as Hiraṇyahasta—and gave him [wealth]. The Vedic citation is: "O Aśvins, bestowing gold-handed [gifts]" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.119.24), and so forth. And likewise... [the verse continues].
1. *ga*-gāthā; *ta1.2.3.6.7.8*-yathā; *ta4.5*-yadvā | 2. *ga-ta1.2.3.7-bha* do not contain "belonging to the *juhotyādi* class.
3. *ga-ta5*-śyāvaṃ śyāmaṃ; *ta1.2.3.6.7.8-bha1.2.4.8*-śyāvaṃ śyā.
You two brought the daughter of Vena, Kamadhū, who kindles desire, as a wife for the seer Vimada;
the scriptural citation is: “You [brought] her to Vimada by means of a chariot” (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10.39.7).
Likewise, having brought back the lost son Viṣṇāpu to the seer Viśvaka, you released him—that is, you gave him back.
‘As if to see a lost animal,’ is the Vedic citation (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.116.23).

The daughter of the lightning, the thundering one, the one-footed goat, the upholder of heaven, the river, the waters of the ocean—all the gods, together with Sarasvatī, with their inspired thoughts and wisdom, hear my words. pāvīravī | tanyatuḥ | ekapād | ajaḥ | divaḥ | dhartā | sindhuḥ | āpaḥ | samudriyaḥ | viśve | devāsaḥ | śṛṇvan | vacāṃsi | me | sarasvatī | saha | dhībhiḥ | purandhyā || 13 ||

The daughter of lightning (*pāvīravī*), the wielder of weapons, the thundering one, the roaring one— such is the voice of the middle region (*mādhyamikā vāk*). Likewise, the supporter, the sustainer of heaven (*divaḥ dhartā*), the unborn one (*aja*) who moves as a single being (*ekapāt*), the deity known by that name, the river (*sindhuḥ*), and the oceanic waters (*samudriyā āpaḥ*)—
the ocean being the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*), and the waters existing therein.
In the phrase “*samudrādvādraḥ*,” the suffix *gha* is used in the sense of origin (*bhavārtha*).

May the All-Gods (*viśve devāḥ*), joined with their mental activities (*dhībhiḥ*)—that is, their ritual actions—and accompanied by manifold wisdom (*purandhyā*), as well as Sarasvatī, hear my words, that is, the hymns (*vacāṃsi*) to be spoken.
One should reflect upon the *Nirukta* passage beginning with: “The *pavi* is the arrowhead, because it pierces the body” (*Nirukta* 12.30).

May all the gods, together with their insights and with wisdom, the worshipful ones of Manu, the immortal ones who know the cosmic order (ṛta), who accompany the gift, who attend upon us, who find the light of heaven, and whose voices are heavenly—may they graciously accept this sacred prayer, this well-spoken hymn. 14. All the gods, together with their insights and with wisdom, the worshipful ones of Manu, the immortal ones who know the cosmic order (ṛta), who accompany the gift, who attend upon us, who find the light of heaven, and whose voices are heavenly—may they graciously accept this sacred prayer, this well-spoken hymn. 14.

Accompanied by wisdom (*dhībhiḥ*) and actions (*karmabhiḥ*), joined with insight (*purandhyā*), worthy of worship (*yajatrāḥ*) in the sacrifice of man (*manuṣyasya yajñe*), immortal (*amṛtāḥ*)—free from the nature of death—knowers of Truth (*ṛtajñāḥ*), partakers of the offered oblation (*rātipācaḥ*), approaching the sacrifice from all sides (*abhipācaḥ*), gathering together, finders of light (*svarvidaḥ*), all the gods (*viśve devāḥ*) beginning with Indra, may they enjoy (*juṣerata*) all our songs (*svaḥ giraḥ*), this great sacred word (*brahma mahat*), this well-spoken hymn (*sūktaṃ*), or this praise (*stomaṃ*) well-offered along with the mantra.
The root *jup* means "to love" and "to serve.
It belongs to the Taudādika class and is anudātta (unaccented).
The absence of the substitution of *ras* for *liṭ* in *likhi* is due to Vedic usage;
the augment *ruṭ* is applied by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).

Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who have pervaded all the worlds. May they grant us wide-striding [space]; and do you, O gods, protect us always with blessings. 15. devān | vasiṣṭhaḥ | amṛtān | vavande | ye | viśvā | bhuvanāni | pratasthuḥ | te | naḥ | rāsantām | urugāyam | adha | yūyam | pāta | svastibhiḥ | sadā | naḥ || 15 ||
Vasiṣṭha: This sage, born of the lineage of Vasiṣṭha, paid homage to—the immortal, deathless—gods; thus he praised them.
Those who have set out toward all worlds, who dwell over all beings with their own splendor on every side.
1. *ga-ta-bha* read *yuvām*. 2. *ta-bha* read *liṭi*. 3. *ta-bha* does not have “*viśvā*”. 4. *ga-ta1.2.3-bha* read *bhuvanā bhuvanāni*;
or [it means] “they stand firm. This is a form from the root *siṣṭ* (from *pra-siṣṭ*) in the *liṭ* tense.
O gods, may you grant us on this day abundant food, which brings wide renown;
O gods, do you always protect us with your auspicious aids.
"Devān huve" is a hymn (*sūkta*) of five verses (*ṛc*) consisting of fifteen *ṛcs*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) and other details are as before.
It is cataloged as "Devān huve."
On the fifth day of both the *pṛṣṭhya* and *abhiplava* six-day periods, this *vaiśvadeva* [śastra] contains the *nivid*.
It is stated in the Sūtra: "The *vaiśvadeva* consists of the four verses beginning with 'iheha vaḥ' and ending with 'devān huve'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.5).

I invoke the gods of vast renown for our well-being—those makers of light, the wise ones of the sacrifice; those who have increased further, the all-knowing, with Indra as their chief, the immortals who strengthen the cosmic order. 1. I invoke the gods of vast renown for our well-being—those makers of light, the wise ones of the sacrifice; those who have increased further, the all-knowing, with Indra as their chief, the immortals who strengthen the cosmic order. 1.

I invoke for the well-being— that is, for the non-destruction and the completion of this sacrifice without obstacle— those gods who possess great renown, who provide abundant food, who are the makers of light (the creators of the splendor known as the Ādityas),
and who are highly wise. They are the possessors of all wealth,
with Indra as their chief— that is, those among whom Indra is the foremost.
The meaning is "having Indra as their leader.

Being immortal (*amṛtāḥ*), free from the nature of death; increasing through the sacrifice (*vṛtāvṛdhaḥ*); those gods (*vyai devāḥ*) have increased (*vavṛdhuḥ*) and continue to increase (*vavṛdhuḥ*) exceedingly (*prataram*).

Impelled by Indra, directed by Varuṇa, those who have attained a share of the light of the sun—within the host of Maruts, in the assembly, we fix our thought; in the bountiful one, the wise sages have generated the sacrifice. Impelled by Indra, directed by Varuṇa, those who have attained a share of the light of the sun—within the host of Maruts, in the assembly, we fix our thought; in the bountiful one, the wise sages have generated the sacrifice. 2. Impelled by Indra, directed by Varuṇa, those who have attained a share of the light of the sun—within the host of Maruts, in the assembly, we fix our thought; in the bountiful one, the wise sages have generated the sacrifice. 2.

Impelled by Indra—urged by him toward their respective tasks—and instructed by Varuṇa—advised and approved by Varuṇa—those Maruts have attained the portion, the share worthy of being enjoyed, of the radiant Sūrya, the impeller of all in their own duties;
that is to say, they abide presiding over the sun.
In the host of Maruts— belonging to the bountiful Indra, who shatters the hosts of enemies— we fix, we offer, we compose our *manman*, the meditative hymn worthy of praise.
Furthermore, the wise patrons (*sūrayaḥ*), the sacrificers, for that very purpose, generate the sacrifice.
They perform [the rites] for the offering of oblations to them.

May Indra with the Vasus protect our household; may Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter. May the god Rudra with the Rudras be gracious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the Grāsis quicken us for prosperity. Indra, with the Vasus, may he protect our home; may Aditi with the Ādityas grant us refuge. May the divine Rudra with the Rudras be merciful to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the Grāsis inspire us toward well-being.
Accompanied by the Vasus—those gods of that name—may Indra protect (*pari pātu*) our *gaya*, which here means "house";
for it is that which is to be reached, or where one sings (*gāyate*) and sounds forth; thus, *gaya* is the house.
May he guard it completely.
Thus he says: May the Mother of the Gods (Devamātā),
together with the gods, grant us (naḥ) protection (śarma)— that is, happiness.
Furthermore, may the radiant Rudra, together with the Rudras—his own sons, the Maruts—be gracious to us; that is, may he grant us happiness.
[The root] *mṛḍ* means "to gladden"; the augment *iṭ* is applied according to the rules of the leṭ (subjunctive) mood.
Moreover, may Tvaṣṭṛ, the Lord of Progeny, together with the sisters—the wives of the gods and the meters—gratify us for our well-being, that is, for the prosperity that is to be properly attained.
Aditi, Heaven and Earth, the great Cosmic Order, Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the lofty Sky—
we invoke the divine Ādityas for protection, the Vasus, the Rudras, and Savitṛ of wondrous deeds.

Aditi; Heaven and Earth; the Cosmic Order; the Great One; Indra and Viṣṇu; the Maruts; the Sun; the Vast; the Gods; the Ādityas—we invoke for protection; the Vasus; the Rudras; and Savitṛ, the performer of wondrous deeds. 4.
Aditi, Heaven and Earth—the two great worlds—Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the vast and sovereign Svar (the Sun/Heaven), and these gods who abide everywhere by their own majesty;
we invoke these gods, beginning with the Ādityas, and Savitṛ, whose deeds are excellent, for the sake of protection. We call upon them for our preservation.
May Sarasvant with his prayers, Varuṇa whose laws are firm, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu of great majesty, Vāyu, and the two Aśvins—
the immortals who perform sacred prayer and possess all knowledge— grant us protection, a triple-layered refuge from distress.

Sarasvant, Varuṇa whose laws are firm through holy thoughts, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Mahiman, Vāyu, the Aśvins, those who perform the sacred word, the immortals, the all-knowing—may they grant us a triple-layered protection from sin. 5.

May these gods—Sarasvat, endowed with *dhī* (insights and wisdom), the one whose vows are firm; Varuṇa, whose actions are steadfast; Pūṣan; Viṣṇu, possessed of greatness; Vāyu; the two Aśvins; those who perform sacred acts (*brahmakṛtaḥ*), who perform deeds, or who are givers of food to the singers; the possessors of all wealth (*viśvavedasaḥ*), or possessors of all knowledge; the slayers of sin-forming enemies (*aṃhasaḥ*); and the immortals (*amṛtāḥ*)—may they grant us a triple-protected (*trivarūtham*) shelter (*śarma*), a home with three supports, three chambers, or indeed, a triple-layered protection.
The house which is the means for the sacrifice, wherein the three vessels known as the *droṇakalaśa*, *ādhavanīya*, and *pūtabhṛt* are kept—that is, where they are shared—is [the place].
May they bestow it; "may they grant" (*yaṃsan*) is from the root *yach* in the *leṭ* mood with the augment *sip*.
May the sacrifice be a bull; may the sacrificial objects be bulls; may the gods be bulls, and the preparers of the oblation be bulls.
May Heaven and Earth, the observers of cosmic order, be bulls; may Parjanya be a bull, and the supporters of the world be bulls.

The sacrifice is a bull; may the worthy of worship be bulls; may the gods be bulls; may the preparers of the oblation be bulls. May Heaven and Earth be bulls, observers of the Eternal Law (*ṛtāvarī*); may Parjanya be a bull; may the supporters of the rain-cloud be bulls. ||6||

May this sacrifice of ours be a showerer (*vṛṣan*) of desires; likewise, may the gods who partake in the sacrifice be showerers. Furthermore, may the gods—the officiating priests who perform the praise—be showerers through the act of offering excellent praise, being the causes for the raining down of wealth.

Likewise, let the *haviṣkṛtaḥ*—the performers of the oblations, such as the Adhvaryu and others—be *vṛṣaṇaḥ*, "virile" through their unweariedness, their assistance with mantras, and the offering of the oblations.

Furthermore, let *dyāvāpṛthivī*, heaven and earth, who are *ṛtāvarī*, "possessors of the sacrifice," be *vṛṣaṇā*, "showering down desires" by means of the production of the oblation. (Note: Regarding the variants, *ga* reads *triḥbhūrimi*; *tā1.2.3.6.7.8-bha* reads *triḥkramaṃ*.)
2. tā1.2.3.7-mu-trikakṣaṃ; ta4.5-trikarakṣaṃ | Kaṭha 4-13 Ṛgveda: [Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 2, Varga 13]
May Parjanya, the lord Indra, be the showerer of waters for you. May all the officiating priests, praising the gods with showers of hymns, become showerers [of blessings].
O Agni and Soma, you bulls, for the winning of booty—I invoke you, the bulls, who are highly praised.
You two, whom the bulls have worshipped with the sacrifice to the gods, may you extend to us a triple-layered protection.

O Agni and Soma, you two bulls, for the winning of booty—I address you, the highly praised bulls—who have been worshipped by those who offer oblations to the gods; may you two extend to us a triple-layered protection. 7.
O *vṛṣaṇā*, you two who are habitually showerers [of benefits], *purupraśastā*, praised by many, O *agnīṣomā*, Agni and Soma, I address you—I praise you—for *vājasātaye*, the acquisition of food.
The repetition of "O *vṛṣaṇau*" is for the sake of emphasis.
Those two gods whom the *vṛṣaṇaḥ* priests [serve] through the sacrifice to the gods (*devayajyayā*).
That by which the gods are worshipped is *devayajyā*, meaning sacrifice (*yajña*).
This word is irregularly formed according to the rule "in the Veda, [the suffix] *niṣṭarkya* [is applied].

By means of that, they have sacrificed, they sacrifice, and they honor with oblations—those two well-known [gods]. May they both *vi yaṃsataḥ*, that is, specifically bestow upon us (*naḥ*) a *śarma* (shelter) consisting of threefold protection and having three supports, i.e., a home.

The Kṣatriyas of firm vows, who are the glory of the sacrifices in the performance of the rites, the Bṛhaddivas— the invokers of Agni, observers of Truth, and free from guile— released the waters following the conquest of Vṛtra.

Firm in their vows, the Kṣatriyas, who accomplish the sacrifice, dwelling in the great heaven, the glory of the rites, having Agni as their priest, observers of Truth, and free from guile, released the waters following the conquest of Vṛtra. 8.
They are those who uphold their vows and perform righteous deeds by birth as Kṣatriyas;
or alternatively,
they are those worthy of *kṣatra*, which is power.

*Yajñaniṣkṛtaḥ*: those who effect the departure toward the sacrifice; *bṛhaddivāḥ*: those of great splendor; *adhvarāṇām*: of the sacrifices that have not been obstructed by Rākṣasas; *abhiśriyaḥ*: those who attend to them; *agnihotāraḥ*: those for whom Agni is the invoker; *ṛtasāpaḥ*:
"sāpa" [is derived from] the root *sap*, meaning "to join together."
"Partakers of truth," and for that very reason "harmless," meaning those who do not deceive anyone;
or alternatively,
the suffix *kvip* is added to the root *druh* in the sense of the object (karmaṇi).
They are not to be harmed by anyone.
Such was the power of the gods in the *vṛtratūrya*.
For *vṛtratūrya* is a battle (*saṃgrāma*) in which Vṛtra is struck (*tūryate*) or slain (*hiṃsyate*).
In that [Indra], who is the destroyer of the enemy that obstructs the waters, they released—that is, they caused to flow—the waters, which are the waters.

Generating heaven and earth according to their ordinances, he has brought forth the plants and the holy works. He has filled the mid-region and the sky according to his will; the gods have directed him toward all things.

Heaven and Earth; generating the sacred ordinances; the waters, the plants, and the wide spaces; the holy ones have filled the mid-air and the light for our protection. By their will, the gods have stretched out the warp of the sacrifice. 9.
O gods— Indra and the other deities— having directed yourselves toward Heaven and Earth by means of your own sacred law (*vrata*) and ritual action,

you generated the waters, the purifying streams, the waters themselves, and likewise the plants, as well as the sacrificial trees worthy of sacrifice, such as the *palāśa* and others that grow in the forest.
Furthermore, those gods have filled the entire heaven and the intermediate space with their splendor;
for what purpose? For protection—that is, for defense against enemies and the absence of affliction.

Moreover: 1. *avaśam* [is used] in the introduction of the *kāmya*, *ta*, *bha*, and *mu* [feet]; 2. *ga-trikchadiṣṭakam*; *tā*, 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, and 8 [are used] with the sequence of *bha* and three *tri*s; *ta*4 [is used] with the *triṣṭubh*.
3. There is no [root] *abhi* with *ga*, *ta*, *bha*, or *mu*.
According to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.3.58.3, *māna* [is formed]; the suffix *aṇ* is applied to a factor other than the agent (*akartari kārake*) by the rule "the addition of *vaśaraṇya*."
They thoroughly cleansed that sacrifice within their own bodies, making it perfectly pure and well-adorned.

May the *Ṛbhus*, the upholders of heaven with their skillful hands, and Vāta and Parjanya of the thundering bull, may the waters and the plants further our prayers; may Bhaga, Rāti, and the prize-winning steeds come to my invocation.
May the upholders of heaven, the Ṛbhus with skillful hands, Vāta and Parjanya, the waters, and the plants further our songs. May Bhaga, Rāti, and the swift ones come to my invocation. 10.

The Ṛbhus— the sustainers (*dhartāraḥ*) of heaven (*divaḥ*), shining through truth, gods with beautiful hands (*suhastāḥ*) equipped with the excellent weapon of the thunderbolt— likewise [produced] the great roar (*mahiṣasya tanyataḥ*) of the vast [thunder],
derived from the root *tanu* (to expand) with the suffix *yat* according to the rule *ṛtanyijña*.
May Vāta and Parjanya—the two makers of sound—Vāta and Parjanya, whose effects are water and plants—[may they] further and increase our songs, that is, our hymns of praise;
for the root *tṛ* preceded by *pra* has the sense of increasing.
Likewise, may Rāti (the giver), Bhaga (the one worthy of being honored), Aryaman, and the Vājins [grant us prosperity].
"Fire, wind, and the sun—these indeed are the Vājins," so says the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (1.6.3.9).
May these gods come to my *hava*, that is, my invocation.
The ocean, the rivers, the dust, the atmosphere, Aja Ekapād, the thunder, and the flood;
Ahibudhnya, who hears my words, all the gods, and Sūrya—may they heed me.

The ocean; the rivers; the region; the intermediate space; the unborn; the one-footed; the thunder; the flood; the serpent of the deep; may all these hear my words—the All-Gods and also Sūrya—[and] my vital core. 11.

°Samudraḥ: the ocean, characterized by flowing, with its waters streaming forth; °Sindhuḥ: the river of that name; °Antarikṣam: the intermediate space, situated or dwelling between heaven and earth; °Rajaḥ: the middle world; °Aja Ekapāt:

the "Unborn One-footed," the deity so named who, though unborn, alone ripens [all things]; °Arṇavaḥ: the watery one; °Tanayitnuḥ: the thunderer, the cloud; °Budhnyaḥ: the one born of the intermediate space; °Ahiḥ: the serpent—may these deities, bearing these names, each individually hear my words, the hymns to be spoken, as I recite them.
Moreover, O wise ones, may all the gods, the Viśvedevas, hear my hymns of praise.
May we be yours, O Manu-sages, for the feast of the gods; lead our sacrifice forward in a straight path. O Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, you bounteous givers, quicken these prayers being recited.
May we be yours, O men, for the feast of the gods. Lead our sacrifice forward in a straight path. O Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, you bounteous givers, quicken these prayers that are being recited. 12.

O gods, we humans are yours; for your *devavīti*—that sacrifice in which there is the eating (*vīti*) of the gods—may we be its performers. Therefore, may you [accomplish] our sacrifice with excellence.
The word *supo* is a substitute for the case-ending.

O Ādityas, o Rudras—meaning the Maruts, the sons of Rudra—o Sudānavas—those of beautiful gifts—and o Vasus: bring forth, that is, perform excellently and most highly, this auspicious and beneficial [work]. O [gods], quicken—that is, gladden—these *brahmāṇi*, these hymns being recited.

1. Ga-tara. 3.6.7.8-bha-parjanya-vāyu. At the *bhasoryāma*, for the *atiriktoktha* of the *acchāvāka*, "O divine Hotṛs" (*adaivyā hotārā*) is the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*). And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The concluding verse is 'Both indeed now, the two divine Hotṛs, the first domestic priests' (*ubhā u nūnaṃ daivyā hotārā prathamā purohitā*)," [Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 9.11].
I follow rightly the path of Truth, along with the two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first appointed ones.
We pray to the Lord of the Field, our neighbor, and to all the immortal gods who rise at the break of dawn.

The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first appointed priests—I follow their path of Truth straight on. We pray to the Lord of the Field, our neighbor, and to all the immortal gods who never neglect us. 13.

"I follow" (anvemi)—that is, I go after—the two "first" (prathamā), that is, the primary, "divine" (daivyā), that is, belonging to the gods, "Purohitas," that is, the two Purohitas placed in front, the two "Hotṛs" named Avenant, namely Agni and Āditya, as they carry the oblation.
Then, I follow "the path of Ṛta," that is, the path of sacrifice, "well" (sādhuyā), meaning auspiciously and without forgetfulness.

Immediately after, we pray to the "neighbor" (prativeśam), who dwells nearby; to the "protector of the field" (kṣetrasya patim), whose name is such-and-such; and to all the "immortal" (amṛtān) gods, who are free from the nature of death and who are never negligent—we entreat them for wealth.

Like the Vasiṣṭhas, they have fashioned their speech like that of a father, praising the gods like seers for our well-being. Like affectionate kinsmen, come to our desire; O gods, shake down wealth upon us.

Like Vasiṣṭhas, they have raised their voices like a father; praising the gods like seers for our well-being. Like affectionate kinsmen who have come to fulfill our desire, O gods, shake down wealth upon us here and now. 14.

Like ancient seers, like ṛṣis of old, the Vasiṣṭhas—those seers born of the Vasiṣṭha clan—praising and lauding the gods, have fashioned their speech, that is, their hymn of praise, for well-being and non-destruction, just as Vasiṣṭha did.
(This is from the *luṅ* tense of the root *kṛ*, with the elision of *cli* according to the rule "mantra ghasa").
O gods, having grasped our desire and come hither, shake down—that is, bring toward us—the wealth consisting of cattle and other riches right here.
In this regard, there is an illustration:

"Just as delighted kinsmen and relatives, being themselves joyful, urge their own kin toward wealth; in the same way, through [your] giving and by means of praise, urge us toward wealth like a kinsman"—this is the intended meaning.
Vasiṣṭha has paid homage to the immortal gods who have extended themselves over all the worlds. May they grant us wide-striding space; and do you, O gods, protect us ever with your blessings.
Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who have extended themselves over all worlds; may they grant us wide space today. Do you protect us always with blessings. 15.
This verse has already been explained previously.
The seventh hymn, consisting of twelve verses beginning with "imāṃ dhiyam," is the seerly composition of Āṅgirasa Āsyā, composed in the Triṣṭubh meter.
This and the following [hymns] have Bṛhaspati as their deity. Thus it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: "Imāṃ dhiyam: twelve verses; Āsyā; dedicated to Bṛhaspati."
In the *ābhīra* meters (1.
ta1.2.3.4.5.6.8-bha1.2.6.7.8), the first two [syllables] are short; in the *ta7-mu* meter, the first two are short.
In the *ga4-ta1.2.3.6.7.8* meter, the word "anvemi" does not exist.
In the Pluvikeyu and Ukthya sacrifices, when there is an increase in the *stoma*, this hymn is for the purpose of insertion (*āvāpa*) by the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
And it is prescribed: "The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites] 'imāṃ dhiyam' and the two hymns 'viṣṇonuṃ kam'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.9).
Our father discovered this seven-headed, lofty hymn, born of the Eternal Law (Ṛta).
Indeed, Ayāsya, the friend of all people, generated its fourth part while reciting the liturgy for Indra.
Our father discovered this seven-headed, lofty hymn, born of Eternal Order (*ṛta*). Indeed, the one common to all people, Ayāsya, brought it forth while reciting a song of praise for Indra. 1.
Regarding this, they relate an ancient history: In former times, it is said, there was a sage named Aṅgiras who obtained a son, Bṛhaspati;
he became the domestic priest of Indra for the purpose of instructing the gods in what is beneficial.
Once, his cows were carried off by the Asuras known as the Paṇis and brought to the city of Vala; there they were placed in three locations shrouded in darkness.

Then, dispatched by Indra to search for them, Bṛhaspati arrived there with Aṅgiras. Having generated the Sun so that he might see the cows situated in their cave, he slew the Asura named Vala and his followers, the Paṇis, and brought back the cows.
This will be demonstrated here.

And thus, the meaning of this verse is as follows: [I praise] the *dhi* (intellect), the sustainer of actions, which has seven heads— that is, it possesses seven heads in the form of the seven groups of Maruts who serve as its primary limbs—
or alternatively, it has seven heads consisting of the seven meters (*chandas*).

Our father Aṅgiras found—meaning he obtained—this great (*bṛhatī*) body of ours, which was born for the sake of sacrifice (*yajña*), being one who has brought forth truth (*ṛtaprajātā*). The meaning is that he obtained a son, Bṛhaspati, the contemplator of ritual acts (*karman*).
As the Brāhmaṇa states: "Those who were Aṅgiras became the Aṅgirases; when Aṅgiras, having been extinguished, blazed up again, he became Bṛhaspati" (AiB 3.34).

Likewise, the one who is beneficial to all people (*viśvajanya*) produced even the fourth essence; he produced it for Indra, the Lord, and Bṛhaspati—for Indra indeed—while reciting the hymn of praise (*uktha*). This seer named Ayāsya said: "Our father has already performed this for us in the past."

Proclaiming the *ṛta*, meditating on the straight path, the sons of Heaven, the heroes of the Asura, the Aṅgirases, establishing the inspired singer as their station, conceived the first ordinance of the sacrifice.
Proclaiming the *ṛta*, meditating upon the straight path, the sons of Dyaus, the heroes of the Asura, the Aṅgirases, assuming the inspired state, conceived the first foundation of the sacrifice.

Proclaiming the *ṛta*—the hymn that has become truth—and praising it; meditating upon the straight and auspicious, that is, contemplating their sacred rites; [these are] the sons of Agni Aṅgiras, the son of the radiant Asura of heaven.
For it has been said that "the Aṅgirases were born from Aṅgiras" (*aṅgiresyo jātāḥ*), and according to the Nirukta (3.17), "Aṅgiras was among the embers."

These heroic ones, possessing courageous wisdom, being the Angirases, uphold through their ritual action that station called Bṛhaspati—the wise one who instructs and sustains the abode of sacrifice—and thus, from the very beginning, they first of all meditate upon him, that is, they praise him;
for this station which is Bṛhaspati is indeed the instructor.
The *yājyā* for the oblation of the *devasū* sacrifice, dedicated to Bṛhaspati Vācaspati, is the verse beginning with “Like swans” (*haṃsairiva*).
This is also prescribed in the Sūtra: “O Bṛhaspati, the first beginning of speech... like swans with their chattering friends” (*Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 4.11).
Like swans, with his speaking companions, Bṛhaspati, the wise one, has cast off the bonds of mortal men; he has bestowed [the light] and, knowing [the way], has praised aloud and sung forth.
1. *ga-ta-teṣām*—search for these. 2. *ga-ta-bha*—the word "svit" is not present. 3. *ga-ta-bhara*. 4.6.8—*ajanayat iti*; *bha1.7*—*iti*. 4. *ga4*—*putrāsaḥ*. 5. *ta-bha*—*kārakam*.
Like swans, with his friends, speaking loudly, Bṛhaspati, casting asunder the stone-made bonds, bellowing toward the cows, has praised them forth; and being wise, he has sung aloud. (3)

Like swans with sweet voices, accompanied by friends who have become his companions, and by the Maruts shouting exceedingly, Bṛhaspati proceeds—casting aside, scattering, and loosening the stone-made enclosures, the places of the cows, the Vandanas, the Kanyakas, the Āpyas, and the Asuras—while bellowing toward them, desiring to recover the cattle that had been carried off by the Paṇis. Accompanied by the chanters who are speaking loudly and praising him excessively, he roars toward the cows—that is, he utters aloud the words characterized as hymns;
moreover, he began the prelude (*prāstaut*).
Seated with his friends at the commencement of the ritual, he begins the singing of the *Sāman* melody.
The wise one, knowing all, having become the Udgātṛ priest, sang upward; he sings the Udgītha for the gods, that is, he praises them.
With two [verses] he drove out the filler; with one, the cows standing in the cave at the bridge of Ṛta.
Bṛhaspati, seeking light in the darkness, drove forth those three who were facing away.

Downward with two, forward with one—Bṛhaspati, seeking light in the darkness, drove forth the cows standing in the cave at the boundary of Cosmic Order; for he has indeed disclosed the threefold dawns. 4.
The Paṇis called out for the cows; they placed them in three locations:
from below, standing at the boundary of the darkness of *ṛta*, they drove forth with two locations the cows that were staying in secret hiding places;
then, from beyond—that is, from the highest point—they caused the cows situated there to emerge with one location.
He says that very thing:
Bṛhaspati, desiring to create light in that darkness, drove out—pulled forth—the rays of light (uṣas) that were situated there;
he made them manifest.
In this manner, he indeed opened wide these three gates of the Asuras;
for from the root *vṛ* (to open), in the *luṅ* tense, the *cli* suffix is elided by the rule "in mantras, *ghas* etc.
(*mantre ghasa*), and the augment *aṭ* is applied by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
Fearing for his city, he cut through the three [fortresses] together from the western side of the ocean;
Bṛhaspati found the dawn, the sun, and the cows, like the thundering sky.
Out of fear, he shattered the stronghold; he cut out three [treasures] together from the ocean. Bṛhaspati discovered the sun, the cow, and the light, like the thundering sky. 5.

That Bṛhaspati, having stood with his upper and lower garments, having shattered and torn asunder this city of the Asuras which was turned away and facing the west, forcibly from the ocean—the Asura in the form of a cloud—simultaneously brought forth together these three: the dawn, the sun, and the earth; he cut them out from those places enveloped in darkness. Having produced the sun that appears later in time, he caused the cattle to be swallowed up [by light].
He has found the *arka*, the hymn worthy of praise, and makes it known.
How so?
Just as the sky remains while thundering, making a sound.

2. In manuscript ga: *upaśayena sthitvā*; in manuscript bha: *upa upaśayena sthitvā*; in manuscript su: *upaśayena sthitvā*.

Indra, with his roar like a hand, cut apart Vala, the protector of the strongholds, as if with a weapon. Desiring the *āśira* mixture along with the Maruts who possess dripping ornaments, he caused Paṇi to weep and carried off the cows. Indra, the Lord Bṛhaspati, with his roar—which stands like a hand equipped with weapons—cut apart Vala, the Asura who guarded the cows that yield milk from the strongholds; he tore him asunder. Furthermore, desiring the *āśira* (the mixture of milk and soma) together with the Maruts—who are "sweat-dripping" (*svedāñci*), meaning they have flowing ornaments—he caused Paṇi, this Asura named the follower of Vala, to weep, that is, he destroyed him. Then he carried away the cows seized by him.

With his true, radiant, and wealth-bestowing companions, he shattered Vala, the holder of the cattle. As the Lord of Prayer (Brahmaṇaspati), with his bull-like, boar-like, and sweat-heated [Maruts], he attained the treasure. He, with his true, radiant, and wealth-bestowing companions, shattered Vala, the holder of the cattle. As the Lord of Prayer—the sovereign of the hymns characterized by Ṛk, Yajus, and Sāman—he, with his bull-like, rain-showering, boar-like bringers of the desirable water, and with the Maruts who are heated by the sacrificial fire (or who carry flowing waters, or who go toward the sacrifice), attained the treasure consisting of cattle.

Seeking the cows, they impelled Bṛhaspati with their thoughts—the Lord of Cows—with a truthful mind. Bṛhaspati, by means of those Maruts who protect the cattle from mutual reproach and who are his own companions, released the ruddy cows upward. Seeking the cattle stolen by the Paṇis, those Maruts approached them, joined with a mind that was true—that is, directed toward the reality of the goal—and with their own ritual actions (*dhībhiḥ*), they impelled Bṛhaspati, the Lord of Cows, desiring him with the thought: "Let us make him the master of the recovery of the cattle. And Bṛhaspati, by means of those Maruts—who are called *mitho'vadyapebhiḥ* because they come together with one another while protecting the cattle from being subject to reproach (*avadya*)—and who are his own companions (*svayugbhiḥ*), meaning those who are spontaneously united with him, he released the ruddy cows (*usrīyāḥ*) upward, driving them out from the mountain.
Exalting him with auspicious thoughts, like a lion roaring in his dwelling place,
we rejoice after Bṛhaspati— the bull, the victorious one— in every battle for the sake of heroes.
1. *ta-bha-sādhukara* | 2. *ga-ta1.2.3.6.7.8-ma- ‘svedāñbhiḥ’ is not present*.

Him (*tam*), increasing with auspicious thoughts (*mati'bhiḥ śivābhiḥ*), like a mist (*miham'iva*), roaring (*nānadatam*) while standing in the firmament (*sudha'sthai*), Bṛhaspati, the bull (*vṛṣaṇam*), in the winning of heroes (*śūra'sātau*), in every battle (*bhare'bhare*), following the exhilaration (*anu madam*), the victorious one (*jiṣṇum*). 9.
"Together with the gods"—elsewhere [the term] *sadhastha* refers to the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*).

In that [space], we celebrate with auspicious and beautiful hymns of praise *anu madam* (in accordance with joy) that *Bṛhaspati*, who is like a roaring lion, sounding again and again, the showerer of desires (*vṛṣaṇam*), the victorious (*jiṣṇum*), while magnifying him for the sake of great choice wealth in every battle (*bhare-bhare*)—a battle to be sought after by heroes (*śūrasātau*). Alternatively, this may be construed as referring to the worshippers themselves.

When he won the prize of every form, and ascended to the highest heaven; then, magnifying Bṛhaspati the bull, they who were manifold, bearing light with their mouths, [attained all things]. 10. When | the prize | he won | of every form | and to the sky | he ascended | the highest | all | Bṛhaspati | the bull | magnifying | being manifold | bearing | light | with their mouths || 10 ||

When that Bṛhaspati, at whatever time, partakes of *vāja*—food characterized by cattle—which is *viśvarūpa*, having manifold forms; or when, possessing draft animals, he ascends to *dyām*, the heavenly world, or otherwise ascends to higher stations (*uttarāṇi... sadya sthānāni*); then the gods strengthen Bṛhaspati, the showerer (*vṛṣaṇam*), with their mouths (*āsā*). (Note: Regarding the form *arukṣat*: it is derived from the root *ruh* in the *laṅ* tense; the substitution of *śala* for *ślu* and the suffix *kas* apply according to Pāṇini 3.1.45: *śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ*.)
Likewise, you who are present in various directions, bearing and maintaining the light, even the gods offer praise.

Grant a true blessing, O bestower of vitality; protect even the humble singer with your own aids. Let all adversaries fall behind us. Hear that, O Heaven and Earth, you who encompass all. satyām | āśiṣam | kṛṇuta | vayaḥ-dhe | kīrim | cit | hi | artha | svebhiḥ | evaiḥ | paścā | mṛdhaḥ | apa | bhavantu | viśvāḥ | tat | rodasī iti | śṛṇutam | viśva-minve iti viśvam-inve || 11 ||
O Bṛhaspati and the other gods, bestowers of vitality, make our prayer—the hymn of praise—true, that is, in accordance with reality, for the sake of establishing a storehouse of food.
Likewise, protect and preserve me, the singer, by means of your own movements;
"hi" is used here as a particle of emphasis.
The word *paścā* is a Vedic particle established by the rule *paścā ca chandasi* (Pāṇini 5.3.33).
*Paścāt* means "afterwards"; *viśvāḥ* means "all"; and *mṛdhaḥ* means "enemies" or "obstacles. [O Agni,] you shall destroy them; let them go away, that is, let them perish.
O Viśvaminve, you two who gladden the universe, O Rodasī, Heaven and Earth, hear these words spoken by us.

Indra, the great one, split asunder the head of the great ocean, of Arbuda; he slew the serpent and set the seven rivers flowing. O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us! 12. Indra, the great one, split asunder the head of the great ocean, of Arbuda; he slew the serpent and set the seven rivers flowing. O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us! 12.
Indra, the lord, endowed with great majesty, together with Bṛhaspati, split asunder and severed the head— the summit— of the great, watery Arbuda, the cloud.
This is what is said.
He slew the dragon, the invincible enemy who obstructed the waters; he struck him down.
Thereupon, he released the flowing rivers—the waters that are wont to flow—or rather, [the waters themselves].
He caused the rivers, such as the Gaṅgā, numbering so many,
to flow toward the ocean, or rather, he released them.
Now, regarding the one performed by direct perception:
O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us—favor us.
The eighth hymn, consisting of twelve verses beginning with "udprataḥ," has the same seer and other details as the preceding ones. It is introduced by the words "udprataḥ."
This hymn belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin during the Uktha [stotra].
It is stated in the Sūtra: "pra maṃ hiṣṭhāya... acchā ma indram" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 6.1).
Like birds guarding their young from above, like the roars of clouds from below,
like waves breaking against the mountains, the singers have shouted praises to Bṛhaspati.
Arising at dawn, we—protecting ourselves from the enemy—like the roars of thunderclouds or waves breaking from the mountain, have raised our hymns toward Bṛhaspati, crushing [the foes]. 1.

The birds (*vayaḥ*) are those that rise up from the water (*ud-prataḥ*); from that [state], the farmers (*kṛpīvalāḥ*) protect themselves. The particle *na* is used in the sense of comparison (*upamā-arthe*):
they cry out just as [the birds do].

And just as the sounds of a thundering cloud— that which repeatedly emits sound— arise like those of a mass of clouds; and furthermore, just as the waves, the masses of water fallen and issued forth from the mountains— that is, from the clouds— become exultant and resound, so do the singers,
the worshippers who offer praise, chant toward Bṛhaspati.
‘Now, in the sense of praising.’
Reaching toward us with his rays like a prize-seeking steed, he has led away Aryaman as if he were Bhaga;
like Mitra among men, he anoints the two lords of splendor; O Bṛhaspati, bring forth the swift steeds for the sake of booty in the contest for wealth.

Like Bhaga, the descendant of Aṅgiras, approaching with cattle, has led Arthaman to his goal among the people. Like Mitra, he anoints the husband and wife; O Bṛhaspati, incite us to victory like a swift horse in the race.

The son of Aṅgiras, the descendant of Aṅgiras, pervading with his own splendor, like the god Bhaga himself, Bṛhaspati has led—the leader of praise—along with the cattle, to the one who offers praise; he unites them. Just as Mitra unites his own rays among the people in the inhabited land, so too does he anoint—that is, he brings together—the husband and wife;
by his own power, he establishes them there. This is the meaning.
O Bṛhaspati, send forth and establish the swift, far-reaching rays for the sake of strength among your praisers;
just as warriors bring together swift, far-reaching horses in battle, so do thou.
The Adhvaryus have brought forth these desirable, vigorous, and radiant waters— splendid, of blameless form—
from the mountains, as Bṛhaspati winnowed grain from the chaff.

Excellent are they, noble, hospitable, vigorous, desirable, golden-hued, and of faultless form. Bṛhaspati, having overcome [the obstacles] from the mountains, has driven out the cows, as one winnows grain from the chaff.
1. *ga-ta-bha-mu-bhagaiva* (like one who has gone to the share of the gods). 2. *ga-ta-bha-mu-yathā āśviniva* (just as the two Aśvins [have come]).

7. *Sādhvaryāḥ*: the leader (*netrī*) of the virtuous, auspicious, and flowing waters; 7. *atithinīḥ*: constantly moving; 7. *iṣvirāḥ*: desirable; 7. *spārhāḥ*: yearned for; 7. *suvarṇāḥ*: possessing beautiful white and other colors; 7. *anavadyarūpāḥ*: of blameless form, i.e., of excellent form—these 7. *gāḥ* (cows), having 7. *vittvā* (having found) them from 7. *parvatebhyaḥ* (the mountains belonging to Vala), 7. *upa* (nearby) 7. *devasamīpe* (in the presence of the gods), 7. *nirvapati* (he pours out/brings forth).
In this regard, there is an illustration: "like barley.
Just as one, having taken barley from usurers, pours it out [as an offering].
The root *ḍuvap* means "to sow" or "to plant. This is a form in the perfect tense (*liṭ*).
Alternatively:
Having brought the waters—the cows endowed with qualities such as being easy to travel upon—from the mountains, that is, from the clouds, he rains everywhere.

Sprinkling the honeyed womb of Cosmic Order, Bṛhaspati—casting down a meteor from heaven like a flame—drew forth the cows from the rock as if from the earth; he rent the skin apart like a hide. āpruṣāṇan | madhunā | ṛtasya | yonim | avakṣipan | arkaḥ | ulkām'iva | dyoḥ | bṛhaspatiḥ | uddharan | aśmanaḥ | gāḥ | bhūmyāḥ | ut | dā'iva | vi | tvacam | bibheda ||4||

"Sprinkling with honey and water," that is, pouring [it] directly upon the earth; for the root *pruṣ* (in the sense of "to sprinkle, to moisten, to fill") is used here. By way of grammatical anomaly (*vyatyaya*), there is the substitution of *śa* for the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*).

Scattering—that is, dispersing for the sake of rain—the cloud, the source of *ṛta* (the cosmic order) and water; like Bṛhaspati, the one worthy of praise (*arka*), who draws up a meteor from the sky (*dyo*) as it were; seeing the cows stolen by the Paṇis and situated upon the mountain (*aśman*) with its clefts, he drew them up—that is, caused them to go upward—and split open the skin of the earth, namely their hooves, having divided their purpose.
The meaning is that he made the cows known everywhere.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
O Deva, just as the rain-cloud pierces the earth with the water of its downpour, so too [does it act].

With light, he has driven away the darkness from the mid-air; as the wind drives out the *śīpāla* grass, so Bṛhaspati, having seized them, has driven the cows hither from Vala, as the wind drives the clouds. 5. With light, the darkness, from the mid-air, the water-snake, like the *śīpāla*, the wind drove out; Bṛhaspati, having touched, of Vala, like a cloud, the wind, he made [them] come, the cows. 5.
Bṛhaspati, by means of light—that is, by means of the sun produced within the mountain cleft—drove away, that is, caused the darkness to depart, from the atmosphere.
Therein is an illustration:
as a wolf [drives away] a jackal.
Just as the wind drives away the *śīpāla* (water-weed) from the water, so it was.
Then, having touched [the ground] and reflected—having determined that "cows are standing here"—he brought the cows, which were within the mountain that was his own domain, out from all sides.
How so?
Like a cloud: just as the wind scatters a cloud—a mass of vapor—situated in the atmosphere, so too [is it].

When Bṛhaspati shattered the strength of the devouring Vala with his fire-heated rays and hymns, as a tongue devours what is set before it, he made manifest the hidden wealth of the cows. When Bṛhaspati shattered the strength of the devouring Vala with his fire-heated rays and hymns, as a tongue devours what is set before it, he made manifest the hidden wealth of the cows.

1. Due to the attainment [of this], for that very reason they are desirable (*spārhā*); [the reading *ta-aspārhāḥ* means] they are longed for by all. In other manuscripts, the phrase "desirable, longed for" (*spārhāḥ spṛhaṇīyāḥ*) does not appear. 2. According to Ga4, Ta, Bha1.2.4.9.8, [it is] now being drunk.
The word *pīyati* has the meaning of "to injure.
When— at which time— the weapon (*jasu*) of the injurer, *vala*, breaks (*bheta*),
by what means?
He pierces [the darkness] with rays that are like nectar, like fires, swift-moving, and worthy of worship— alternatively, with mantras—
and furthermore, with his teeth; the substitution of *dadbh-* for the word *danta-* occurs according to the rule beginning with "padakṣomāsaḥ."

Just as the tongue eats food that has been set before it by the teeth, so too when he seized—that is, ate and slew—the one named Vala who was surrounded on the mountain by the Paṇis, he then made manifest the hidden hoards of the *ustriyās*, the cows that had been carried off by them. He caused them to appear.
There, Bṛhaspati found and obtained the cows by means of the *uṣas* (dawns) for the purpose of seeing them in the mountain cleft.
Having thus obtained the Āditya and Agni, he drove away the darkness excessively with his radiant, worshipful splendor.
Then, by force, he brought out those cows from the mountain—the source (*parvan*) of the *vala*, which was surrounded by cattle and had the body of a cow.
An illustration for taking by force:
it is like extracting the marrow from a bone; just as they extract the marrow from a bone with great difficulty, so too [is this].
Like a full lake drained of its waters, Bṛhaspati took pity on the forests and the cows;
he performed an act beyond imitation, such that the sun and moon rise from each other.

Like snow, full, stolen; the forests; by Bṛhaspati; he took pity; Vala; the cows; the incomparable; "not again"—so he made it, since Sūrya and Māsa move together in alternation. Just as with snow, as if full of leaves—O Agni, that face of yours, the mass of rays, which Manu, so named, kindles thoroughly nearby with oblations, I, Sumitra, so named, kindle thoroughly.
(The root *jinvi* means "to shine" or "to kindle").
In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], there is elision (*lup*) due to the *kit* designation according to the rule "after *hṛ*, *bhū*, and *bhavati*.
Let this very mass of rays, which is both that and this, become ever-new (*navīyaḥ*) and ever-fresh (*navanaraḥ*).
O Thou, shine forth (*śoca*) so as to be rich (*revat*), that is, endowed with wealth.
As such, do you accept and enjoy our songs, our hymns of praise;
as such, do you rend *vāja*, the strength of the enemy.
Likewise, bestow upon me here *śravaḥ*, food.
O Agni, whom Vadhryaśva, having praised you before, kindled with fuel—be pleased with this [offering] of ours.
Be a protector of our dwellings and a guardian of our bodies; protect this gift which is yours among us.
Thee,
O Agni, today.
The people are called *agnayaḥ* because they go toward [the fires];
from them you have won back the treasures (*vasūni*)—such as cattle and other wealth—produced on the mountain, which were beneficial to them, having conquered them from the enemies.
Likewise, you have completely conquered the *dāsas* created by the powerful ones, and the *vṛtras*, the afflictions created by the *asura-dāsas*.
The meaning is that you have killed them;
it is a form in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) from the root *ji* (to conquer).

O Śūra, you who are the subduer of men, overcome—the word *pṛtanāyūn* here lacks the *l* augment by Vedic license—those who attack, those who desire battle; overwhelm them! Even though the suffix *śnas* is prescribed [by Pāṇini 7.1.3] in forms such as *aśvāghasyāt*, it occurs here through metrical variation (*vyatyaya*).
With a long thread, with many skillful fingers, the clever one, possessing a thousandfold strength and a hundred songs,
being cleansed by men among the radiant ones, shines forth among the pious Sumitras.

Long-fibered, with great oxen—this Agni is a thousandfold stallion, a hundredfold leader, skillful, radiant among the radiant ones. Being cleansed by men among the well-disposed friends, shine forth among those who seek the gods. 7.
He has long threads;
those by which he extends [the sacrifice] are the "threads," namely the hymns of praise and so forth.
He possesses abundant praise and is the great bull.
The bull is the sprinkler, the ray;

released with abundant rays, he is the "thousandfold impregnator" (sahasrastarīḥ), having many coverings in the form of oblations (havīrūpa-bahucchādanaḥ). He has a hundred ways (śatanīthaḥ), meaning he is led in many ways through the doors of the Āhavanīya and other fires. He is the skillful (ṛbhvā) one, the great, and among the luminous (dyumatsu), the most radiant (dyumān). This Agni, being cleansed and adorned by men—the leaders of rites and those who have overcome their enemies—is made beautiful. [The root] *mṛj* is used in the sense of purification and adornment.
As such, shine—be radiant—for us, who are seekers of the gods, who desire the gods, and who are good friends;
"dīdayaḥ" means "shine," as it is a verb denoting the act of shining.
For you, O Jātavedas, is the cow that yields milk well; like one who never fails, she is ever-present and abundant.
You, O Agni, are kindled by men who bestow sacrificial gifts, by the pious Sumitras who seek the gods.

O Jātavedas, you are like a well-milking cow that yields inexhaustible nourishment at all times. O Agni, you are kindled by men who possess sacrificial gifts, by those with good friends, and by those devoted to the gods. 8.
O Jātavedas, O Agni, in you there exists a certain well-yielding cow (*sudughā*)—one that yields milk excellently—which serves as the means for the oblation. Of what nature is she?

She is "unfailing" (*asaścata*), meaning she is not joined with or connected to anything due to the absence of fixed location; yet she is "endowed with a companion" (*samanā*), that is, united with her kin. She is the speech of the intermediate region (*mādhyamikī vāk*) in the form of a cow, yielding nectar (*amṛta*). The sense is that such a cow exists within you, O Vaiśvānara.

Such as you are, you are kindled—that is, made to blaze—with oblations by us, who are like men who lead the ritual action, who possess sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*), who are like officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) in their obligation to give, who are seekers of the gods, and who are well-disposed friends desiring the divine.
Even the immortal gods, O Jātavedas, have proclaimed thy greatness and thy power,
when the human tribes came to thee, asking, as thou wast strengthened by the men who aided thee.
Even the immortal gods, O Jātavedas, son of Vadhryaśva, have proclaimed your greatness when the human tribes came to consult you; you, with the men who were strengthened by you, achieved victory. 9.

O Jātavedas, O Agni Vādhryaśva, even the immortal gods—those very deities—proclaim your greatness. When the human clans, the descendants of Manu, came together in consultation with the gods, inquiring, "Who indeed shall slay the Asuras? and so forth, then you, along with the leaders of all, the gods who were strengthened by you, conquered those who obstructed the ritual work. You have won the victory.
Like a father his son, Vadhryaśva has embraced you, O Agni, as he attends upon you;
enjoying his fuel, O Most Youthful One, you have consumed even many offerings.

Like a father his son, you have placed him in your lap, O Agni; Vadhryaśva served you with devotion. O youngest one, taking pleasure in this fuel of his, you have granted him many boons, even though he was but a wood-gatherer.
O Agni, Vadhryaśva, my father, while serving you— performing the rite of attendance— in the lap of the earth, that is, upon the high altar (uttaravedi),
has maintained or nourished [you] with oblations.
How so?
Just as a father places his son near him or nourishes him;
[as expressed by] the root *bhṛñ* in the sense of "supporting" and "nourishing."
In the *laṅ* tense, when the *guṇa* substitution has been applied, there is the elision of *tip* by the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal*.

O *ayaviṣṭha*, most youthful one! And furthermore (*uta*), being one who enjoys (*juṣāṇaḥ*) the fuel-stick (*samidham*) of either this Vadhryaśva or of me, my father, you have destroyed (*avanoḥ*) even the ancient, powerful (*vrādhataḥ*) enemies—those who cause oppression (*bādhakān*).
The root *vanati* is used in the sense of "to injure" and belongs to the *bhūvādigaṇa*.
The suffix *up* occurs by way of transposition.
Eternal Agni has ever conquered the enemies of Dhyashva with those who have pressed the Soma;
O you of wondrous luster, you have consumed even the assembly, and you have shattered even the powerful obstructors.

Eternal is Agni; with his men who have pressed the Soma, he has conquered the enemies of Vadhryaśva. O you of wondrous luster, you have burned up even the assembly; O impetuous one, you have shattered even the mighty foe.
That Agni, by means of those men— the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*)— who possess the pressed Soma (*sutasomavat*),
that is,
those by whom the Soma has been pressed (the suffix *-mat* being explanatory), has at all times (*śaśvat*) conquered his enemies.

Now, regarding the term *pratyakṣa*: O Agni, you who possess manifold splendor (*acitrabhāno*), or rather, you whose radiance is worthy of being sought after (*cāyanīya-dīsiman*), even though you are present in every battle (*samanaṃ cit*)— *samana* being a name for battle.
He too you burnt up with your own splendors.
Then your praiser Vadhryaśva—himself growing strong, even as one who causes others to grow—crushed, that is, cut down, the swelling or increasing aggressor, turning him face downward;
or rather, you yourself crushed him.
Having turned [the hand] face-down, it is called *abhinaḥ*.
This form is the same for both the first and middle fingers.
This Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra, kindled from of old by Vyaśva, is to be addressed with reverence;
as such, O Vrādhyaśva, overcome our arrogant foes, whether they be unrelated or even kinsmen.

This Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra, belonging to Vadhryaśva, has been kindled from of old; he is to be addressed with reverence. O Lord of the great steeds, trample down those who defy us—whether they be strangers or kinsmen. 12.
"This Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra and destroyer of enemies, has been kindled—that is, intensely illuminated—by the oblation of Vadhryaśva from time immemorial, from of old.
Likewise, he is to be invoked with reverence along with salutation.

O Vrādhyaśva, O Agni produced by friction in the lineage of Vadhryaśva, do you overcome and subdue our enemies who are unrelated to us (ajāmīn), as well as those who are related but arrogant and injurious (śardhataḥ vijāmīn)."
1. *ga4-ta-bha1.4.6.7.8-mu-liḍi*.
The second hymn, consisting of eleven verses beginning with “*imāṃ me*,” is the seer’s work of Sumitra Vādhryaśva and is composed in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
Its deities for each verse are Tanūnapāt, Narāśaṃsa, and Samidh, respectively.
And thus it has been introduced: “*imāṃ me ekādaśāpram*. This *Āprī* hymn belongs to the animal sacrifice of those belonging to the Vādhryaśva lineage.
And it is stated in the sūtra: “*samiddho adya* for all, or according to the ṛṣi” (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 1.2).

O Agni, enjoy this fuel of mine; at the place of *iḷā*, graciously accept the ladle full of ghee. On the summit of the earth, on the day of fair days, be uplifted through the sacrifice to the gods, O you of noble wisdom. *imām me agne samidhaṃ juṣasveḷaspade prati haryā ghṛtācīm | varṣman pṛthivyāḥ sudinatve ahāmūdhrdho bhava sukrato devayajyā || 1 ||*
"O Agni, in the place of *iḷā*, in the place of *iḷā*.
The Brāhmaṇa states: "This indeed is the place of *iḷā*, namely the navel of the *uttaravedī*.
[Thus,] upon the *uttaravedī*, enjoy—that is, accept—this fuel-stick of mine.
Likewise, desire—that is, long for—the needle that anoints itself with clarified butter (ghṛtācī).

Furthermore, O Sukrato (one of excellent wisdom), at the height (varṣman) of the earth—in the elevated region previously mentioned—on account of the excellence of the days, and by means of the sacrifice to the gods (devayajyā), rise upward, becoming lofty with your flames.

May Narāśaṃsa, who goes at the head of the gods, come hither with his horses of every form; along the path of Truth, with reverence, may he, the most divine among gods, well prepare the sacrificial food for the gods. 2. ā | devānām | agrayāvā | iha | yātu | narāśaṃsaḥ | viśvarūpebhiḥ | aśvaiḥ | ṛtasya | pathā | namasā | miyedhaḥ | devebhyaḥ | devatamaḥ | supūdat || 2 ||
Narāśaṃsa is the foremost among the gods, the one who goes at the head.

According to the rule "in the case of *vanaspati* and others, both [members] simultaneously [retain their original accent]," there is simultaneous preservation of the original accents (*prakṛtisvara*) for both the preceding and following words.
May this fire, named Narāśaṃsa—who is to be praised by men—come here to this sacrifice together with horses of various forms, such as the red ones (*rohit*) and others.

And having come, may that Agni—the most excellent among the gods, worthy of sacrifice, beneficial to the ritual, or worthy of praise—by means of conveying the oblation, along the path of *ṛta* (the cosmic order) of the sacrifice, together with our bowing hymn of praise (*namas*), send forth the well-prepared oblation to the gods, Indra and the others.

Men, possessing oblations, evermore praise Agni for his office as messenger. With your carrying horses and with a well-rolling chariot, bring the gods; sit down here as the Hotṛ-priest. 3. Evermore. They praise. For the office of messenger. Possessing oblations. Men. Agni. With the carrying ones. With horses. Well-rolling. With a chariot. The gods. Bring. Sit down. Here. As the Hotṛ-priest. 3.

"Evermore"—that is, perpetually and eternally—men who possess oblations, that is, men who have prepared the sacrificial offerings, praise Agni for the sake of his office as messenger. [The suffix] *yat* is applied according to the rule "the portion and the function of a messenger. For the sake of the messenger's task, characterized by the carrying of the oblation, they praise him on that account.

Thus praised, you, O Vahni (the bearer), with your most excellent horses and with your well-rolling, easy-turning chariot, bring hither the gods, Indra and the others; carry them toward our sacrifice and cause them to arrive. Then, becoming the Hotṛ priest, sit down here in this sacrifice.
Ṛgveda: [Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 2, Varga 22] (Kra. 4-14, 520)
May the god-loved sacrificial grass spread out wide; may its long stalk be fragrant for us.
O divine Barhis, with a mind free from malice, worship the longing gods, with Indra as their chief.

Spread out, O divine Barhis, that which is dear to the gods, extending crosswise and long in its length; may it be fragrant for us. With a mind free from malice, O god, worship the longing gods, with Indra as their chief. 4.
"O Barhis, beloved by the gods and frequented by the gods— this Barhis, which is low-lying and horizontal for those born in the transverse direction—
may it spread out, may it be especially extended; and likewise, may this long one be lengthened."
From the word *dīrgha*, with the suffix *amenic*, there is the substitution of *drāghi* according to the rule "priyasthira... and so forth;
the letter *a* is replaced by *i* through a transposition of phonemes (*varṇavyatyaya*), and subsequently, the final *l* is elided.
May it be endowed with length.
May our *barhis*—our sacrificial grass—be fragrant, made sweet by the placement of oblations such as Soma.
O radiant *deva*, O *barhis* named thus, [act] without malice!
"Hela" is a name for anger.
With a mind free from anger, worship—that is, honor and sacrifice to—the gods who have Indra as their chief, who desire the oblations.
Touching the ridge of heaven, spread yourselves out more widely according to the measure of the earth.
Yearning with greatness, O great ones, place the divine Agni upon your chariot like a charioteer.
Touching the ridge of heaven, or expanding wide with the measure of the earth, O longing Doors, uphold with your greatness and grandeur the divine chariot, you who desire the chariot. 5.
"O you goddesses named Advaras, you are from heaven.
The word "vā" has the sense of "and. "And touch the ridge of heaven," meaning the most elevated, the wider place; that is, become uplifted.
Because of the rule "the first [word] in a *ca-vā-yoga* is not subject to *nighāta*," there is no suppression of the accent.
"By as much as is the measure of the earth, by that much measure take your stand; spread yourselves out.
Desiring the gods, you who are longing, seek the chariot.
The substitution of *su* for *jas* is according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.

O truthful ones who desire chariots, uphold—hold fast to—the divine, shining chariot, which is the means of delight, presided over by great gods through its greatness (*mahinā* = *mahimnā*). Uphold it!
May the two goddesses, the daughters of heaven, the well-fashioned Dawn and Night, sit down in their proper place. May the longing gods sit upon your wide, well-favored lap, O you who yearn for them.

The two goddesses, the daughters of Heaven, the well-fashioned Dawn and Night, shall sit down in their place. May the longing gods sit upon you both, who are longing, in your spacious and auspicious lap.
May the two goddesses, Dawn and Night—the two daughters of Heaven, shining brightly, of beautiful form—sit down in their place, the seat of the sacrifice.
O longing ones, full of desire; O fortunate ones, possessed of splendid wealth; O two goddesses, may the gods, desiring the oblations, sit down upon your broad lap, your nearby station.
Upright is the pressing-stone, kindled with great flames; the dear abodes are in the lap of Aditi.
O two priests, appointed at this sacrifice, you who are most wise, do you two win wealth through the ritual.

1. There is the substitution of *ga*, *ta*, and *drāgh* in such cases as [the rule] beginning with "it. 2. The term *bhavān* does not exist. 3. In *ga*, *ta*, and *mu*, and also in the case of the earth (*pṛthivī*).

Upright, a protector, great, Agni is kindled in the lap of Aditi, in her dear abodes. O two priests, the two preceptors at this sacrifice, you who are most wise, bestow wealth upon us through worship. 7.

When the pressing-stone (*grāvan*) stands upright for the pressing of Soma, and when the great fire (*bṛhad agniḥ*), kindled by oblations, is fully ignited; and when the beloved abodes (*dhāmāni*)—those which delight the gods through the offering of Soma and other oblations and which sustain the sacrificial offerings—are placed within the lap (*upasthe*) of Aditi, that is, upon the sacrificial seat of the earth; at that time, O two priests, Daityas, and Purohitas, you two Hotṛs are stationed in front, being most wise (*viduṣṭarā*). [The vowel change *saṃprasāraṇa* is Vedic.]
